answer: Before an agent may submit a bid, make it solve a memory-hard puzzle bound to that auction and its public key. The auction nonce prevents saving answers for later, while the key binding prevents reusing one solution across aliases. In an ocean of bids for a garden robot contract, even a whisper of extra influence requires another full puzzle. Spawning names is cheap, but submitting through them consumes RAM bandwidth and energy each time. Tune difficulty below the value of honest bids; hardware advantages and rented botnets remain limits.
